newsitem.title: USA: Hughes Electronics net income rises.
newsitem.headline: Hughes Electronics net income rises.

text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp. said Tuesday profits jumped 77 percent in the second quarter and that the planned spinoff of its defense business will be tax-free under a key ruling from the Internal Revenue Service.
Hughes said net income rose to $541.4 million, or $1.35 a share, in the quarter, from $306.6 million, or 77 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose 18 percent to $4.76 billion from $4.05 billion.

Earnings for both periods include a $30.6 million gain related to General Motors Corp.'s original purchase of Hughes. Results for the latest quarter include a gain of $318 million, or 80 cents a share, from Hughes' acquisition of 71 percent of PanAmSat Corp., a satellite systems operator, in May.
Operating profits, excluding gains and adjustments, were $339.1 million, down from $450.4 million in the 1996 quarter.
Separately, General Motors said it received a ruling from the Internal Revenue Service on Monday that GM's planned spinoff of Hughes' defense operations would be tax-free to GM and its stockholders.

The tax-free status was crucial to the deal. Without it, General Motors would have faced a huge capital gains tax bill that could have ended the transaction. GM said in January it would spin off Hughes' defense operations to GM and Hughes stockholders and then sell the business to Raytheon Co. in a deal worth $9.5 billion.

As part of the deal, GM will transfer Delco Electronics from Hughes to GM's Delphi Automotive Systems and will recapitalize GM Class H common stock into a stock linked to the telecommunications and space businesses of Hughes.

GM said it will seek General Motors and Hughes shareholder approval for the deals in the fourth quarter. The merger of the Hughes defense business and Raytheon is also subject to approval by regulators and Raytheon stockholders.
